title: Attention runtime byte-heatmap and FlashAttention v3 interaction report
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary:
We are seeing intermittent latency regressions and memory pressure spikes when routing to FlashAttention v3 on certain long-context conversational workloads. Existing telemetry shows increased token latency and occasional out-of-memory soft-fails that recover after a short backoff. This ticket builds a lightweight diagnostic: a per-request, per-layer byte-heatmap that correlates memory allocation peaks, kernel selection decisions (v2 vs v3 path), and per-token latency contribution.

Goals:
1) Implement an end-to-end minimal instrumentation layer that emits a compact byte-heatmap event for every request sampled at 1% or when a routing anomaly occurs. The event will capture (as labels) model, layout, sequence_length, layer_index, selected_kernel_tag, workspace_bytes_peak, kv_cache_peak, and per-token-ms for prefill vs decode.
2) Produce an automated analysis job that aggregates heatmaps into a small set of patterns and surfaces rules: e.g. "layer N chooses v3 and workspace > X causing decode jitter", or "layer M falls back to v2 under fragmentation and latency increases by Y ms".
3) Ship a human-readable investigation report with recommended mitigations (scheduler knobs, eviction heuristics, tiny v3 layout shim) and one small runtime change (opt-in telemetry flag and a conservative v3 gating threshold).

Success criteria / Acceptance:
- Heatmap events are emitted without increasing p50 latency by more than 1% (sampled mode).
- The analysis job flags at least three distinct interaction patterns on our Canary workload set.
- Concrete mitigation (gating threshold) validated in canary reducing regression occurrences by >= 65%.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change kernel implementations or do large refactors of the allocator. It is focused on observability and a conservative throttling/gating recommendation.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- We prefer a compact heatmap over verbose raw traces to keep telemetry ingestion costs low. The heatmap is per-layer compact integer counts + peak bytes; full per-op traces are available via separate debug flags.
- We will instrument at the runtime boundary (kernel scheduler) to avoid deep changes in FlashAttention code paths. This reduces instrumentation fidelity slightly but keeps risk low.
- Sampling at 1% balances signal vs cost; anomaly-triggered captures (OOM, fallback-to-v2, >2x expected latency) will bypass sampling.

Telemetry schema (compact):
- event_type: attn_byte_heatmap
- tags: [model, layout, seq_len_bucket, layer_index, kernel_choice, request_id]
- metrics: [workspace_peak_bytes, kv_cache_peak_bytes, prefill_ms, decode_ms_per_token_bucket]

Rollout plan:
- Create opt-in runtime config: telemetry.attn_heatmap.enabled = off by default; enable for canary namespace and Rooftop canary cluster.
- 1st week: collect data from canary, iterate analysis rules.
- 2nd week: validate gating threshold in canary, run A/B with 0.5% production sampling.
- If validated, schedule follow-up to enable gating for high-risk models in Dedicated pools.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Aisha Khan: Initial spike analysis shows most sample regressions cluster at layers 14-18 for long-context Llama-variant. Decided to keep instrumentation in scheduler to avoid touching flashattn internals.

2026-03-04 — Ethan Chen: POC for heatmap event implemented in runtime/telemetry. Emitted payload is ~320 bytes on average after compression. Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234

2026-03-06 — Design review (Sofia Martinez): Confirmed compact heatmap is acceptable. Requested UX doc in Confluence for how SRE and oncall will interpret flags: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Attn+Heatmap+Playbook

2026-03-09 — QA (Liam Parker): Canary run produced 18K heatmap events over 24h; automated analysis grouped into 4 patterns. Noted a false positive where short microbursts were labeled as 'oom-like' due to allocator metric lag — will add a 50ms smoothing window.

2026-03-11 — Performance (Ethan Chen): Verified sampling at 1% added +0.6% p50 on canary. Triggered captures show rich signal for kernel-choice correlation. Draft mitigation: conservative gating when workspace_peak_bytes > 0.8 * heur_alloc_limit for v3.
2026-03-13 — PM feedback (Ravi Singh): Prioritize gating threshold validation and A/B test. Add a follow-up ticket to surface heatmap patterns in Console per-route dashboard.
2026-03-14 — Action item (Aisha Khan): Prepare canary rollout plan for gating; create ENG-271402 to implement conservative v3 gating and ENG-271403 to add Console visualization.
